title_home: Atlas · A map of every game, on every platform
description_home: Atlas maps video games across platforms: what is well known, what is read about this week, what is coming and which games are alike. Open JSON files, made every day.
description_explore: Browse Atlas: the best known games, the trends and the games coming soon, on the Switch and on Steam.
footer_made: A Boréale project. Code under GPL-3.0, data from open sources.
footer_trademarks: Nintendo Switch, Steam and the games named here are their owners' trademarks. Atlas is not affiliated with them.
hero_title: A map of every game, on every platform.
hero_lede: Atlas charts video games from store to store: which are well known, which are read about this week, which come out soon and which are alike. Plain JSON files, free to use, drawn again every day.
hero_sub: Plain JSON · No account, no key · Made every day
mock_label: A game linked across Switch, Steam, GOG and Xbox by links.json, beside this week's trending games
explore_lede: The best known games, this week's trends and what comes out soon. Choose a game to see everything the files say of it.
platforms_lede: Each platform has a folder of its own, its files in the same formats. A game's ids on every store tie the platforms together.
platform_switch_text: Renown and trends from Wikipedia, series and studios from Wikidata, games alike and editions.
platform_steam_text: Renown from Wikipedia and Steam's reviews, the most played, tags and games alike.
platform_gog_text: The whole GOG catalogue with its reviews.
platform_xbox_text: The Microsoft Store's games, their players' ratings and what is in Game Pass.
platform_3ds_text: The 3DS's games across their regions, with their title ids, from Nlib API and Wikidata.
platform_ps4_text: The PS4's games from Wikidata: release dates, traits and PlayStation Store ids (Sony's terms forbid collecting the store's data).
platform_ps5_text: The PS5's games from Wikidata: release dates, traits and PlayStation Store ids (Sony's terms forbid collecting the store's data).
platform_retro_text: The games no store sells any more, from Wikidata.
files_lede: Every file, its size and the day it was made. A daily file older than two days, or a weekly one older than nine, is marked late.
files_note: Each file has a schema number: new fields may come, an old one keeps its meaning.
file_popular: How well known each game is, its trend this week and its critics' score
file_games: Each game's traits: series, studios, genres, tags, reviews
file_similar: The games most like each one
file_upcoming: The games coming out in the next year
file_editions: Each edition with the game it is one of
file_links: A game's ids on every store, by its Wikidata item
file_index: Every file with its day, size and hash
file_source: What a source answered, kept as collected (the platforms' files are made from it)
use_title: No account, no key, no limit
use_lede: The files are plain JSON. Read them from wherever suits you.
use_cdn_text: The data branch, served by a fast CDN. The address never changes.
use_site_text: The same files, under data/, made again with each run.
use_index_text: index.json gives each file's hash: ask for it once a day, then fetch only the files that changed.
use_releases_text: Every Monday's files are kept for good as a release, each file attested. The latest is always at the same address.
use_formats: Each file's format, field by field, is in the
sources_lede: Only sources that need no account. Each file names its own.
source_wikidata: Games, series, studios, genres, critics, ids on every store
source_pageviews: How often each game's pages are read, in eight languages
source_titledb: The Switch's games, their descriptions and release dates
source_steam: Steam's games, reviews, tags and most played
source_steamspy: Owners and players of Steam games
source_igdb: Themes, keywords and players' ratings, when its keys are set
keys_lede: Everything works without a key. Two optional ones add a little, set as the repository's secrets.
keys_igdb: IGDB, through a Twitch application: themes, keywords, players' ratings and hype.
keys_steam: Steam's full list of apps, beyond the games Wikidata knows.
closing_title: Find your way, game by game
closing_text: The explorer reads the same files: search a game, see what each platform says of it, find the ones like it.
x_noscript: The explorer needs JavaScript. The files themselves are listed on the project's page.
x_error: The data could not be read. Try again in a moment.
x_popular_note: The best known games, from Wikipedia, the critics and the stores' reviews.
x_trending_note: The games read about more this week than in the four before.
x_upcoming_note: The games coming out next, the nearest first.
x_no_name: Name not on the map yet
x_steam_figures: On Steam: {owners} owners or more, {ccu} playing at the last count
x_not_found: This game is not on the map.

status_lede: Each source and each platform from the last run's report: when it was last updated, and how much of it is linked and reviewed. A daily source older than two days, or a weekly one older than nine, is marked late.
status_none: No report yet: it comes with the next run.
status_files: The files, and when each was made
status_sources_lede: What each source gave at its last collection. Late: the last run did not refresh it in time.
status_platforms_lede: Each platform's games, and the share of them that another platform's ids and reviews complete.
